helpHtml:
Clarifications on testimonies

You may not need these clarifications for your first games. If you are unsure about the wording of a Testimony, refer to this page.

TESTIMONIES WITH AND / OR

  • "The Horse and the Bear are lying" is false if at least one of them is telling the truth.
  • "The Panther or the Peacock, or both, are guilty" is false only if both are innocent.

COMPARATIVE TESTIMONIES

"Someone taller than me is guilty" is false if the Suspect giving the testimony is actually the Culprit (and there is only one Culprit).

CASES WITH MULTIPLE CULPRITS

Some Testimonies may refer to just one of the Culprits and still be true:

  • "A herbivore is guilty" is true if at least one Culprit is a herbivore. All herbivores could still be guilty. If the card is true, all you know is that at least one of them is guilty.
  • "A herbivore is guilty" is false if none of the Culprits are herbivores.

TESTIMONIES WITH ONE, TWO AND THREE

Numbers do not indicate an exact count or a maximum. As above, "a" is indefinite rather than an exact number:

  • "A carnivore is guilty" does not mean only one carnivore is guilty. This testimony is not false if two carnivores are guilty (at least one of them is).
  • "Two culprits are lying" does not rule out a third culprit also lying. It is false if only one culprit is lying.
  • "Three adjacent suspects are innocent" is true even if four adjacent suspects are innocent.

TESTIMONIES ABOUT ADJACENT SUSPECTS

Some Testimonies refer to the two Suspects adjacent to the speaker ("A suspect next to me is guilty").
In a case with four Suspects, Suspect 1 (the Panther) is next to Suspect 2 (the Peacock) and Suspect 4 (the Iguana).
"Three adjacent suspects are innocent" does not necessarily include the speaker among those adjacent suspects.
